NB: this file is designed for an LLM reader, not a human. Add it to your
LLM’s context and ask it to explain.

- numbered: sentences, every newline ends one: `.md` whole text; `.py`
  docstrings; `.ipynb` Markdown cells, code-cell docstrings; headings,
  quotes, code, code cells, tables, front matter: unnumbered context
- `await rewrite_review(path)`: two models suggest rewrites, file
  untouched; you choose: `review_apply(path, {n: 'new text'})` or edit
  by hand
- `review_passed(path)`: sentences no model flagged: read them too
  /models miss some
- `template=`:
  [`prompt()`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#prompt)
  prose for people; `prompt('terse')` short reference lines, e.g. a page
  per primitive; `prompt('llm')` files an LLM reads
- needs `pip install slopometer[ai]`

``` python
from fastcore.test import *
from nbdev.config import get_config

## Markdown in reading order

A docstring is Markdown.
[`md_parts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#md_parts)
lists what a reader of its prose sees, in order, as pairs. Each sentence
of a paragraph or list item comes as a
[`Sent`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#sent) paired
with the list marker in front of it, such as `-` or `2.`. The marker is
an empty string when the sentence does not start a list item. A heading,
block quote, code block or table comes as None paired with its text. The
model needs these to follow the document, but it is not asked to rewrite
them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L56"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### md_parts

``` python
def md_parts(
    txt
):
```

*Markdown `txt` in reading order as pairs: a
[`Sent`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#sent) with its
list marker, or None with the text of a heading, block quote, code
block, table or YAML front matter*

This docstring text has a heading, a block quote, a numbered list with a
two-line item, a link, and a fenced block:

```` python
MD = """Widgets for the shop floor.

# Shipping

> Ship it today.

1. Pack the widget.
   Tape the box shut.
2. Call [`ship`](api.md#ship)

```python
ship(w)
```
"""
parts = md_parts(MD)
parts
````

Each [`Sent`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#sent) has
the offsets of its sentence in the text. A newline always ends a
sentence.
[`md_parts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#md_parts)
keeps the spacing inside a line, which preserves the columns in a file
of aligned rows.
[`md_parts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#md_parts)
keeps each link, emphasis, HTML tag and formula whole inside its
sentence, even a link target with spaces in it. The model sees them and
can keep them in its rewrite:

``` python
FENCE = '`'*3
test_eq([(s and s.text, t) for s,t in parts], [('Widgets for the shop floor.', ''), (None, '# Shipping'), (None, '> Ship it today.'),
    ('Pack the widget.', '1. '), ('Tape the box shut.', ''), ('Call [`ship`](api.md#ship)', '2. '), (None, FENCE+'python\nship(w)\n'+FENCE)])
tape = parts[4][0]
test_eq(MD[tape.start:tape.end], 'Tape the box shut.')
test_eq([s.text for s,_ in md_parts('fork    exact clone\nagent   starts with nothing\n')], ['fork    exact clone', 'agent   starts with nothing'])
sp = 'Open [My Report.md](</a/My Project/My Report.md:3>)\n<span class="x">Then</span> close it.'
test_eq([s.text for s,_ in md_parts(sp)], ['Open [My Report.md](</a/My Project/My Report.md:3>)', '<span class="x">Then</span> close it.'])
test_eq([s.text for s,_ in md_parts('\\(x + y\\) is positive.\nThe total is \\(a + b\\)\n')], ['\\(x + y\\) is positive.', 'The total is \\(a + b\\)'])
test_eq(md_parts('# Sum \\(a + b\\)\nIt grows.')[0], (None, '# Sum \\(a + b\\)'))
```

## Docstrings in a Python file

This source has a module docstring with a heading, a block quote and a
numbered list. It also has a function with a one-line docstring, a
method with an indented docstring of two paragraphs, and a method with
none:

``` python
SRC = r'''"""Widgets for the shop floor.

# Shipping

`make` builds a widget. Finished widgets ride to the customer with `ship`.

> Ship it today.

1. Pack the widget.
2. Call `ship`.
"""
def make(spec):
    "Build a widget from `spec`"
    return Widget(spec)

class Widget:
    def __init__(self, spec): self.spec = spec
    def ship(self, addr):
        r"""Post the widget to `addr`.

        The label carries the order number. It raises `ValueError` when `addr` is empty.
        """
        if not addr: raise ValueError(addr)
'''
```

The docstrings to find belong to the module, its functions and its
classes.
[`_named`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_named)
walks the syntax tree and gives each function and class a dotted name,
such as `Widget.ship` for a method.
[`_doclit`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_doclit)
returns the string literal that is a node’s docstring, or None when the
node has no docstring.

``` python
tree = ast.parse(SRC)
test_eq([nm for nm,_ in _named(tree)], ['make', 'Widget', 'Widget.__init__', 'Widget.ship'])
[(nm, bool(_doclit(n))) for nm,n in _docnodes(tree)]
```

[`py_docstrings`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#py_docstrings)
returns each docstring of a Python source as a name, the text, and the
offset of that text in the source. The module docstring comes first,
with the name None. Each function and class follows in source order. A
method has a dotted name such as `Widget.ship`. The text is taken from
the file as written, between the quotes, because a rewrite is later put
back at the same offsets.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L100"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### py_docstrings

``` python
def py_docstrings(
    src
):
```

*Each docstring in Python source `src` as (name, text, offset): the
module’s first, with name None, then each function’s and class’s*

``` python
ds = py_docstrings(SRC)
for nm,t,o in ds: test_eq(SRC[o:o+len(t)], t)
[(nm, t) for nm,t,o in ds]
```

The later lines of a docstring are usually indented to match the code
around them. Markdown would read a paragraph indented by four spaces as
code.
[`_dedent`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_dedent)
removes the indentation that those lines share. It also returns a
function that turns an offset in the result into the offset of the same
character in the original:

``` python
d,back = _dedent('First.\n\n    Second line.\n    ')
test_eq(d, 'First.\n\nSecond line.\n')
test_eq(back(d.index('Second')), 12)
d
```

[`py_docs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#py_docs)
splits each docstring into the parts that
[`md_parts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#md_parts)
returns. The offsets of each sentence are positions in the whole source.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L127"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### py_docs

``` python
def py_docs(
    src
):
```

*Each docstring of Python source `src` as (name, parts): parts are as
[`md_parts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#md_parts)
returns, with sentence offsets that are positions in `src`*

``` python
docs = py_docs(SRC)
docs
```

The second paragraph of the method’s docstring is found, though the file
indents it. The offsets of each
[`Sent`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#sent) are
positions in the source file:

``` python
test_eq([nm for nm,_ in docs], [None, 'make', 'Widget.ship'])
raises = docs[2][1][2][0]
test_eq(raises.text, 'It raises `ValueError` when `addr` is empty.')
test_eq(SRC[raises.start:raises.end], 'It raises `ValueError` when `addr` is empty.')
```

## The input for the model

[`rewrite_input`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrite_input)
writes the text that the model reads. Each docstring starts with a line
that names it: `Module docstring:`, or the name of the function or
class. Prose that is not a docstring has the name `''`. It gets no such
line in a Markdown file. A notebook’s code cells have the name `CODE`.
Each is shown as fenced code with no number, and a `Markdown cell:` line
marks the prose that follows it. Every sentence has a number in square
brackets. The numbers do not restart for each docstring, because an
answer names a sentence by its number alone. A list marker stays in
front of the number of the sentence that starts the item. A line
indented further than the first line of its paragraph is shown with that
extra indentation after its number. Aligned rows then keep their
columns. Headings, block quotes, code blocks and tables have no number.

A module can keep part of its docstring elsewhere and leave a `{name}`
placeholder for it, as `aai_coding.write_docs` does. Pass that text in
`fills`. The line after each sentence with a placeholder then gives the
text that the placeholder stands for.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L141"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### rewrite_input

``` python
def rewrite_input(
    docs, # (name, parts) pairs, as `file_docs` returns
    fills:NoneType=None, # Text that each `{name}` placeholder in the sentences stands for
    skip:NoneType=None, # Regex; a paragraph or list item that it matches gets `[-]` in place of each number
    nums:bool=True, # Number the sentences? False gives the same text with no numbers, as `_related` shows an earlier version
    mod_only:bool=False, # Give `[-]` to the docstrings of functions and classes? For a pyskill, whose module docstring is the skill's text
):
```

*The text a model reads for `docs`: every sentence numbered unless
`skip` matches its paragraph or `mod_only` excludes its docstring, with
each docstring under a line that names it, and each code cell shown as
context*

``` python
inp = rewrite_input(docs)
print(inp)
```

``` python
for o in ('Module docstring:', '# Shipping', '> Ship it today.', '2. [4] Call `ship`.', 'Docstring of `Widget.ship`:', '[8] It raises `ValueError` when `addr` is empty.'):
    assert o in inp.splitlines()
test_eq(rewrite_input([('', parts)]).splitlines()[0], '[0] Widgets for the shop floor.')
filled = rewrite_input([('', md_parts('Avoid these.\n\n1. {hedging}'))], dict(hedging='Hedging. Say what is true.'))
test_eq(filled.splitlines()[-2:], ['1. [1] {hedging}', '  ({hedging} stands for: Hedging. Say what is true.)'])
test_eq(rewrite_input([('', md_parts('fork    exact clone\n        tell: its part\n'))]).splitlines(), ['[0] fork    exact clone', '[1]         tell: its part'])
```

Some lines are reference text that no model should rewrite, such as the
line of key bindings at the top of each page of a manual. Pass `skip`, a
regex, to leave them unnumbered. A paragraph or list item that `skip`
matches gets `[-]` in place of each number, so the model reads it and
has no number to answer with. The other sentences keep their numbers:

``` python
skipped = rewrite_input([('', parts)], skip=r'^Pack').splitlines()
for o in ('1. [-] Pack the widget.', '[-] Tape the box shut.', '2. [3] Call [`ship`](api.md#ship)'): assert o in skipped
skipped
```

A pyskill’s module docstring is the text of the skill, and its other
docstrings document code. `mod_only=True` gives the sentences of those
other docstrings `[-]`, so the model reads them and does not rewrite
them. `nums=False` leaves out every number.
[`_related`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_related)
uses it to show an earlier version of a file in the same form as the
document:

``` python
mo = rewrite_input(docs, mod_only=True).splitlines()
for o in ('[0] Widgets for the shop floor.', '[-] Build a widget from `spec`', '[-] The label carries the order number.'): assert o in mo
plain = rewrite_input(docs, nums=False)
assert '\n1. Pack the widget.' in plain and '[' not in plain
print(plain)
```

## The model’s answer

The prompt asks for one answer per sentence. `7 -` keeps sentence 7.
`7 <text>` replaces it. `7-8 <text>` replaces sentences 7 and 8
together. `7 ? <question>` asks what the sentence means.
`7 ? cut: <why>` and `7 ? lost: <fact>` are questions too, so they need
no parsing of their own.
[`parse_rewrites`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#parse_rewrites)
reads those answers into (first, last, text) triples. It accepts the
number with or without brackets. A line that starts with neither a
number nor a space belongs to no answer, and it is skipped.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L170"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### parse_rewrites

``` python
def parse_rewrites(
    reply
):
```

*The answers of `reply` as (first, last, text) triples: text is `-` to
keep the sentences, starts with `?` for a question, and is otherwise the
rewrite, without the `>` that a model may repeat from a description;
indented lines under an answer are rows of its text*

``` python
reply = """0 -
1 -
2 Call `ship` to post a finished widget to the customer.
[3] -
4 -
5 -
6 -
7 The order number is printed on the label.
8 ? what does it do when `addr` is only spaces"""
ans = parse_rewrites(reply)
test_eq(ans[2:4], [(2, 2, 'Call `ship` to post a finished widget to the customer.'), (3, 3, '-')])
test_eq(parse_rewrites('Here are my answers.\n5-6 One sentence for two.'), [(5, 6, 'One sentence for two.')])
ans[-2:]
```

A model can answer a run with rows, when a table or a list says it
better than a sentence. It writes the number, then each row on a line of
its own, indented.
[`parse_rewrites`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#parse_rewrites)
keeps those lines in the answer. With no text beside the number, the
rows are the whole answer:

``` python
rows = parse_rewrites("""3 -
4-6 Read through the kernel:
    file    `view_file`
    search  `rg`
7-8
    always        `ws-sync`
    code changed  restart
9 -""")
test_eq(rows[1], (4, 6, 'Read through the kernel:\n    file    `view_file`\n    search  `rg`'))
test_eq(rows[2], (7, 8, 'always        `ws-sync`\ncode changed  restart'))
rows[1:3]
```

## Putting the rewrites into the source

A rewrite must not damage the file.
[`same_code`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#same_code)
makes a check for that. The check compares the syntax tree of a new
source with the original’s and ignores what the docstrings say. A
quotation mark that ends a docstring early is one way to fail it:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L190"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### same_code

``` python
def same_code(
    src
):
```

*A function that tells whether another source has the same code as
Python source `src`, whatever its docstrings say*

``` python
ok = same_code(SRC)
assert ok(SRC.replace('Build a widget', 'Make one widget'))
assert not ok(SRC.replace('return Widget(spec)', 'return None'))
assert not ok(SRC.replace('Build a widget', 'Build a "widget"'))
```

[`Rewrites`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrites)
applies the answers. Its `new` attribute is the source with each rewrite
in place of the old sentence. `rows` lists every rewrite and question as
(first, last, kind, old text, new text), for a person to review.
`missing` counts the sentences that got no answer line. An answer that
repeats its sentence unchanged counts as `-`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L215"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Rewrites

``` python
def Rewrites(
    src, # The text that the sentence offsets are positions in
    docs, # (name, parts) pairs, as `py_docs` returns
    answers, # (first, last, text) triples, as `parse_rewrites` returns
    valid:NoneType=None, # Called with the source after each rewrite; a false result leaves that rewrite out
):
```

With the answers above, two sentences are rewritten. The rest of the
file is as it was:

``` python
r = Rewrites(SRC, docs, ans, valid=same_code(SRC))
test_eq([(a, kind) for a,_,kind,*_ in r.rows], [(2, 'AFTER'), (7, 'AFTER'), (8, 'QUESTION')])
assert '`make` builds a widget. Call `ship` to post a finished widget to the customer.\n' in r.new
assert '        The order number is printed on the label. It raises `ValueError` when `addr` is empty.\n' in r.new
assert same_code(SRC)(r.new)
print(r.new)
```

`of` returns the rows of one kind. The display gives the counts, then
each row as the old text and the new:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L249"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Rewrites.\_\_repr\_\_

``` python
def __repr__():
```

*Return repr(self).*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L244"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Rewrites.of

``` python
def of(
    kind
):
```

*The rows of one kind: ‘AFTER’ for a rewrite made, ‘QUESTION’, or ‘LEFT
OUT’ for a rewrite not made*

``` python
test_eq(len(r.of('AFTER')), 2)
r
```

[`Rewrites`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrites)
leaves a rewrite out in three cases. Its range runs across two
docstrings or two paragraphs. Another rewrite already covers one of its
sentences. Or the `valid` check fails. Here the first answer joins a
list item of the module docstring to the docstring of `make`, the second
puts a double quotation mark into a docstring that double quotation
marks enclose, and the last two both cover sentence 2:

``` python
out = Rewrites(SRC, docs, [(4, 5, 'Call `ship` and build a widget.'), (5, 5, 'Build a "widget" from `spec`'), (2, 2, 'Use `ship`.'), (1, 2, 'Use `make` and `ship`.')],
    valid=same_code(SRC))
test_eq([(a, b, kind) for a,b,kind,*_ in out.rows], [(1, 2, 'LEFT OUT'), (2, 2, 'AFTER'), (4, 5, 'LEFT OUT'), (5, 5, 'LEFT OUT')])
test_eq(out.missing, 5)
out
```

## Notebooks

A notebook holds prose in its Markdown cells and docstrings in its code
cells.
[`nb_docs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#nb_docs)
reads both in cell order. A Markdown cell gives its prose under the name
`''`. A code cell gives two things. Its whole source comes first under
the name `CODE`, as context that the model reads and does not answer.
The docstring of each function and class in it follows, numbered. A code
cell that Python cannot parse, such as one with a magic, gives its
source only. Raw cells and empty cells give nothing.

In an nbdev notebook the block quote under the title is the module’s
description.
[`nb_docs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#nb_docs)
numbers its sentences so that the model reviews them, though other block
quotes are context only. A description keeps its `>` marker in the
model’s input. The prompt tells the model to keep such a sentence apart
from the text after it, because listings show the description on its
own.

A
[`Rewrites`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrites)
works on one text.
[`nb_docs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#nb_docs)
therefore also returns the cell sources joined by `SEP`, and the
sentence offsets are positions in that text.
[`_addr`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_addr)
gives each sentence an `addr`, the exhash address of the line it starts
on:

A block quote directly under a title is the description of the page, so
[`_md_parts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_md_parts)
numbers its sentences, whereas any other block quote is context.
[`_cell_docs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_cell_docs)
reads one cell, and
[`nb_docs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#nb_docs)
puts the cells together. In a notebook, a sentence’s `addr` starts with
its cell ID:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L287"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### nb_docs

``` python
def nb_docs(
    nb
):
```

*The cell sources of notebook `nb` joined by `SEP`, and its (name,
parts) pairs: the prose of each Markdown cell, and each code cell’s
source followed by its docstrings; each sentence has its `addr` as cell
ID and line address*

This notebook has a title cell with a description, an exported function,
a prose cell, a cell with a magic, and a raw cell:

``` python
NB = new_nb([mk_cell('# widgets\n\n> Build widgets and ship them to customers.', 'markdown'),
    mk_cell('#| export\ndef make(spec):\n    "Build a widget from `spec`"\n    return Widget(spec)'),
    mk_cell('`make` needs a spec. Finished widgets ride to the customer.', 'markdown'),
    mk_cell('%time make(1)'), mk_cell('Not prose.', 'raw')])
nsrc,ndocs = nb_docs(NB)
ndocs
```

In the input for the model, the description has its `>` marker, each
code cell is fenced, and a `Markdown cell:` line marks where prose
starts again. A model may repeat the `>` in its answer, and
[`parse_rewrites`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#parse_rewrites)
drops it:

``` python
test_eq([nm for nm,_ in ndocs], ['', CODE, 'make', '', CODE])
desc = ndocs[0][1][1][0]
test_eq(nsrc[desc.start:desc.end], 'Build widgets and ship them to customers.')
test_eq(desc.addr, f'{NB.cells[0].id}:{lnhash_at(NB.cells[0].source, 3)}')
ninp = rewrite_input(ndocs)
assert '> [0] Build widgets and ship them to customers.' in ninp
assert '    return Widget(spec)\n```\n\nDocstring of `make`:\n\n[1] Build a widget from `spec`\n\nMarkdown cell:\n\n[2] `make` needs a spec.' in ninp
assert ninp.endswith('```python\n%time make(1)\n```')
test_eq(parse_rewrites('0 > Build and ship widgets.'), [(0, 0, 'Build and ship widgets.')])
print(ninp)
```

A rewrite in a notebook must leave the code of every code cell as it
was.
[`_same_cells`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_same_cells)
makes that check for a `SEP`-joined text:

``` python
nok = _same_cells(NB)
nr = Rewrites(nsrc, ndocs, [(0, 0, 'Build widgets and ship them.'), (1, 1, 'Build a "widget"'), (3, 3, 'We send finished widgets to the customer.')], valid=nok)
test_eq([(a, kind) for a,_,kind,*_ in nr.rows], [(0, 'AFTER'), (1, 'LEFT OUT'), (3, 'AFTER')])
test_eq(nr.new.split(SEP)[0], '# widgets\n\n> Build widgets and ship them.')
nr
```

## Rewriting a file

[`file_docs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#file_docs)
reads a file and returns what the later steps need: the text, the (name,
parts) pairs, and the check that
[`Rewrites`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrites)
runs after each rewrite. A notebook gives the text and pairs that
[`nb_docs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#nb_docs)
returns, with the
[`_same_cells`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_same_cells)
check. A `.py` file gives its docstrings and the
[`same_code`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#same_code)
check. Any other file is read as Markdown and has no check. Its
description is numbered too, as in the summary line under the title of
an `llms.txt` file. Each sentence also gets an `addr`: the exhash
address of the line it starts on, which in a notebook follows the cell
ID.

[`write_new`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#write_new)
writes the `new` text of a
[`Rewrites`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrites)
to a file. For a notebook it reads the notebook at `path` and replaces
the source of each cell.

### file_docs

``` python
def file_docs(
    path
):
```

*The text of the file at `path`, its (name, parts) pairs with a line
address as each sentence’s `addr`, and a `valid` check for
[`Rewrites`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrites):
a notebook’s cells, a `.py` file’s docstrings, or the whole text of any
other file*

``` python
root = get_config().config_path
src,fdocs,valid = file_docs(root/'README.md')
test_eq([nm for nm,_ in fdocs], [''])
test_is(valid, None)
src,fdocs,valid = file_docs(root/'slopometer'/'score.py')
assert valid(src) and fdocs[0][0] is None
first = fdocs[0][1][0][0]
test_eq(first.addr, lnhash_at(src, src[:first.start].count('\n')+1))
first.addr
```

A Markdown file’s description is numbered, and a block quote further
down is not. The description can follow the `NB:` line that a file for a
language model has under its title. YAML front matter is shown without a
number:

``` python
f = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'llms.txt'
f.write_text('---\nname: widgets\n---\n# Widgets\n\nNB: this file is designed for an LLM reader, not a human.\n\n> Widget API. Most shop idioms fail here.\n\n- make: `make(spec)`.\n\n> A later quotation.\n')
inp = rewrite_input(file_docs(f)[1]).splitlines()
for o in ('name: widgets', '> [1] Widget API.', '> [2] Most shop idioms fail here.', '> A later quotation.'): assert o in inp
inp
```

A notebook gives the check for its code cells, and each `addr` starts
with a cell ID:

``` python
src,fdocs,valid = file_docs(root/'nbs'/'00_core.ipynb')
assert valid(src) and fdocs[0][1][1][0].addr.startswith(read_nb(root/'nbs'/'00_core.ipynb').cells[0].id+':')
rewrite_input(fdocs).splitlines()[:3]
```

[`prompt`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#prompt)
returns the prompt that ships with the package. It has a `{document}`
placeholder where the numbered sentences go. The default prompt teaches
full explanatory sentences. `prompt('terse')` is for reference pages
written as short lines, such as the page for each primitive of an array
language. It keeps the default prompt’s answer format and its last
section, and has guidance and examples of its own between them.
`prompt('llm')` is for files that a language model reads, such as an
`llms.txt` file, a skill or a system prompt, written in the dense style
that `aai_coding.write_llms` describes. Every style has two answers that
are questions: `? cut:` for a sentence that the reader does not need,
and `? lost:` for a fact that an earlier version has and this one lacks.
[`_related`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_related)
writes out the files that a caller passes as `context`, for the model to
consult. It puts the file passed as `earlier` last, under a heading that
says it is an earlier version of the document. It shows that file as
[`rewrite_input`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrite_input)
shows the document, without numbers. The model then compares like with
like, and cannot report the code of a `.py` file as a fact that the
docstrings have lost.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L327"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### prompt

``` python
def prompt(
    style:NoneType=None, # Name of a style whose examples replace the default ones, `'terse'` or `'llm'`
):
```

*The rewrite prompt that ships with the package, with a `{document}`
placeholder for the numbered sentences*

Pass a style’s prompt as `template`, as in
`rewrite_review(path, template=prompt('terse'))`. Every style shares the
default prompt’s first and last sections, and the first has both
question answers. The last lines check what
[`_related`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_related)
writes for an earlier version. For a `.py` file that is its docstrings
without numbers, and none of its code:

``` python
p,hdr = prompt(),'# The document'
for style in 'terse','llm':
    t = prompt(style)
    test_eq(t.split('\n# ')[0], p.split('\n# ')[0])
    test_eq(t.split(hdr)[1], p.split(hdr)[1])
assert 'Never turn a terse line into a longer sentence.' in prompt('terse')
for o in '? cut:','? lost:': assert o in p.split('\n# ')[0]
assert _related(None, f).startswith('\n\n# Earlier version of the document') and 'Widget API' in _related(None, f)
(py := f.with_suffix('.py')).write_text(SRC)
early = _related(None, py)
assert '`make` builds a widget.' in early and 'return Widget' not in early and '[1]' not in early
```

[`ask_reply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#ask_reply)
sends the whole file’s input to a model in one call and returns the
reply as text. It uses
[`prompt()`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#prompt)
unless the caller passes another template.
[`rewrite_file`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrite_file)
runs every step on one file and returns a
[`Rewrites`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrites).
It does not write the file.

    skip:NoneType=None, # Regex; a paragraph or list item that it matches gets `[-]` in place of each number

*[`Rewrites`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrites)
for the file at `path`, leaving out any rewrite that would change the
code of a `.py` file or a notebook*

With `GEMINI_API_KEY` set, rewrite one file and write the result
somewhere else:

``` python
rw = await rewrite_file(root/'slopometer'/'score.py')
write_new(root/'slopometer'/'score.py', rw.new, '/tmp/score.rewritten.py')
rw
```

## Two models, read by a person

A model’s rewrite is a suggestion. It can drop a fact, rename a term or
split a sentence that was better whole. In this process the models only
point at sentences, and a person or an agent reads what they said and
writes the final text.
[`compare`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#compare)
prepares that reading. It takes each model’s answers under the model’s
name. The first line counts the sentences, and for each model the runs
it rewrote and the questions it asked. Answers whose sentence ranges
overlap are grouped into one run. For each run, it gives the address of
the first sentence, the original text, and then each model’s answer.
Models whose answers differ only in case, spacing or punctuation share a
line. A model that kept the sentences shows `-`.

With `now`, the sentences of the file after editing, each run also gets
a `NOW:` line with the text that stands there. `NOW: -` means that the
run reads as it did.

[`_now`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_now)
finds what stands in the edited file where each run of original
sentences was. It lines up the two lists of sentences with `difflib` and
returns None for a run that reads as it did.

[`compare`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#compare)
builds the text:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L399"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### compare

``` python
def compare(
    docs, # (name, parts) pairs of the original, as `file_docs` returns
    answers, # Each model's name with its answers, as `parse_rewrites` returns them
    now:NoneType=None, # The sentences of the file after editing
    code:bool=False, # Show a notebook's code cell under the first run that explains it?
    brief:bool=False, # Keep only the runs that a model asked about or that every model changed?
    pending:bool=False, # Keep only the runs that read as they did before editing? Needs `now`
):
```

*Text for review: counts, then each run of sentences in `docs` that a
model changed, with its address, the original, each answer, and with
`now` what stands there after editing*

Here a second model answers the same file as `ans` above. It joins
sentences 1 and 2, keeps sentence 7 and repeats sentence 4 unchanged,
which counts as keeping it:

``` python
ans2 = parse_rewrites("""1-2 `make` builds a widget and `ship` posts it to the customer.
4 Call `ship`.
7 -""")
cmp = compare(docs, dict(first=ans, second=ans2))
assert '1-2 ORIGINAL: `make` builds a widget. Finished widgets ride to the customer with `ship`.\n  FIRST [2]: Call `ship` to post' in cmp
assert '  SECOND [1-2]: `make` builds a widget and `ship` posts it to the customer.' in cmp
assert '7 ORIGINAL: The label carries the order number.\n  FIRST [7]: The order number is printed on the label.\n  SECOND: -' in cmp
assert '4 ORIGINAL' not in cmp
print(cmp)
```

A long comparison is quicker to read in two passes. `brief=True` keeps
only the runs that a model asked a question about or that every model
changed. Here the second model kept sentence 7, so that run is left out:

``` python
short = compare(docs, dict(first=ans, second=ans2), brief=True)
assert short.startswith('9 sentences.') and 'Shown: 2 of 3 runs.' in short and '7 ORIGINAL' not in short
print(short)
```

A file’s review files go to one folder, which is `review_dir(path)`
under XDG state unless you pass `out`. The folder keeps the `orig` copy,
which is the file before its first review. Each review then writes to a
numbered folder of its own inside that folder, `1` for the first review.
A later review therefore keeps the replies of the earlier ones. A
numbered folder holds the `reviewed` copy, which is the file as that
review numbered it, and the input, the replies and the comparison.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L437"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### review_dir

``` python
def review_dir(
    path
):
```

*The folder under XDG state that holds the review files for the file at
`path`*

[`_answers`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_answers)
reads the replies that one review saved.
[`_numbers_ok`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_numbers_ok)
checks that this version of the package numbers the file’s sentences as
that review did, because a reply’s numbers mean nothing otherwise:

[`rewrite_review`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrite_review)
asks each model in `asks` about one file, all at once, with no system
message. `ASKS` names the two models we use and the reasoning effort for
each. It changes nothing in the file itself. It saves a copy of the
file, the numbered input, each model’s reply as returned, and the
comparison, which it also returns. Give it a list of files and it
reviews them together and returns one comparison for each.

[`review_diff`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_diff)
compares the file with the `orig` copy, and a later review of the same
file leaves that copy alone unless you pass `fresh=True`. When the file
differs from that copy, a later review also gives the copy to the models
as the earlier version, so that they can answer `? lost:` for a fact
that an edit dropped. Pass `earlier` to name another file, such as the
original of a file that you edited before its first review. The sentence
numbers in
[`review_apply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_apply)
and
[`review_report`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_report)
are those of the latest review, unless you pass `n` to name an earlier
one.

`fills`, `skip` and `mod_only` go to
[`rewrite_input`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrite_input).
Pass `mod_only=True` for a pyskill. Pass `context` to give the models
files to consult, such as the code that a Markdown document describes.
Their contents follow the document in the prompt. A long comparison is
quicker to read in two passes. `brief=True` returns only the runs that a
model asked a question about or that every model changed, and the whole
comparison is still written to the folder. `code=True` prints each
notebook code cell under the first run that explains it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L488"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### rewrite_review

``` python
async def rewrite_review(
    path, # File to review, or a list of them: Markdown, a notebook, or a `.py` file for its docstrings
    out:NoneType=None, # Folder to write to; `review_dir(path)` if None
    template:NoneType=None, # Prompt with a `{document}` placeholder; `prompt()` if None
    asks:dict={'carbon': ('gemini/models/gemini-4-carbon', 'low'), 'sol': ('gpt-6.1-sol', 'medium')}, # Name of each answer and its (model, effort)
    fills:NoneType=None, # Text that each `{name}` placeholder in the sentences stands for
    context:NoneType=None, # Files that the models can consult, such as the code that a document describes
    code:bool=False, # Show each notebook code cell under the first run that explains it?
    brief:bool=False, # Return only the runs that a model asked about or that every model changed?
    fresh:bool=False, # Save the file as a new original? The original that it replaces moves into the folder of the latest review
    skip:NoneType=None, # Regex; a paragraph or list item that it matches gets `[-]` in place of each number
    earlier:NoneType=None, # File that holds an earlier version, for `? lost:` answers; the original that the first review saved if None and the file has changed since
    mod_only:bool=False, # Give `[-]` to the docstrings of functions and classes? For a pyskill, whose module docstring is the skill's text
):
```

*Ask each model in `asks` about the file at `path`; write the original
to `out`, and a copy of the file, the input, each reply and their
[`compare`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#compare)
text to a new numbered folder in `out`; return that text, or one text
for each file of a list; `brief` shortens what is returned, not what is
written*

With `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` set, review one file:

``` python
print(await rewrite_review(root/'README.md'))
```

Here the two sets of answers above have reviewed a file, and one
sentence has since been edited by hand. The review folder holds the
original. Its folder `1` holds the first review’s copy of the file and
both replies, as
[`rewrite_review`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrite_review)
would have written them:

``` python
f,out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'widgets.py',Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
(out/'widgets.orig.py').write_text(SRC)
(d1 := out/'1').mkdir()
(d1/'widgets.reviewed.py').write_text(SRC)
(d1/'widgets.first.answer.txt').write_text(reply)
(d1/'widgets.second.answer.txt').write_text('1-2 `make` builds a widget and `ship` posts it to the customer.\n7 the order number is printed on the label')
f.write_text(SRC.replace('The label carries the order number.', 'The order number is printed on the label.'))
```

[`review_apply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_apply)
makes the edits for you. Give it the new text for each sentence, keyed
by the sentence’s number in the comparison, by a (first, last) pair for
a run, or by the old text itself. Numbers are those of the latest
review, or of review `n`, and they still work after earlier edits have
moved the sentences. An old text can be one sentence or a run of
neighbouring ones, and it must occur exactly once. The call finds the
cell and line itself. It writes nothing unless every edit can be made: a
number that names a sentence you have already edited, an old text that
is missing, and an edit that would change code each raise a `ValueError`
that lists every failure. A notebook is validated before it is written.
Numbers from a review that an older version of the package made can name
the wrong sentences. The call refuses those too, and old texts still
work as keys.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L520"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### review_apply

``` python
def review_apply(
    path, # File to edit
    edits, # New text for each sentence or run, or an empty one to delete it; a key is a number or (first, last) pair from the comparison, or the old text itself
    out:NoneType=None, # Folder that `rewrite_review` wrote to; `review_dir(path)` if None
    n:NoneType=None, # Review whose numbers the keys use, counting from 1; the latest if None
):
```

*Put each new text of `edits` into the file at `path` in place of the
sentences that its key names; if any edit cannot be made, raise
`ValueError` that lists them all, and write nothing*

Here one call replaces the run of sentences 1 and 2, using their numbers
from the comparison:

``` python
msg = review_apply(f, {(1, 2): '`make` builds a widget and `ship` posts it to the customer.'}, out)
assert '`make` builds a widget and `ship` posts it to the customer.\n' in f.read_text()
msg
```

Sentence 7 was edited by hand above, so its number no longer names a
sentence in the file. The call fails, and the edit beside it is not
written either:

``` python
before = f.read_text()
test_fail(lambda: review_apply(f, {7: 'Labels have order numbers.', 'Call `ship`.': 'Then call `ship`.'}, out), contains='7: not in the review, or edited since')
test_eq(f.read_text(), before)
```

An empty new text deletes the sentences that its key names.
[`review_apply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_apply)
also removes the space between them and the next sentence of their
paragraph, or else the space after the previous sentence. It removes
space on the same line first, which leaves each aligned row on its own
line. When a paragraph or list item loses every sentence,
[`review_apply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_apply)
removes its lines and leaves no extra blank line. This file has no
review. Its keys are numbers in the file as it stands:

``` python
MDX = 'Alpha one. Beta two. Gamma three.\nDelta four.\n\n- Item one.\n- Item two.\n  Item two more.\n\nx   row one. row two.\ny   row three.\n'
md = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'notes.md'
def cut(*ks):
    md.write_text(MDX)
    review_apply(md, {k: '' for k in ks}, md.parent/'reviews')
    return md.read_text()
test_eq(cut(1).splitlines()[0], 'Alpha one. Gamma three.')
test_eq(cut(0).splitlines()[0], 'Beta two. Gamma three.')
test_eq(cut(2, 3), MDX.replace(' Gamma three.\nDelta four.', ''))
test_eq(cut(4), MDX.replace('- Item one.\n', ''))
test_eq(cut(5), MDX.replace('Item two.\n  ', ''))
test_eq(cut(8), MDX.replace(' row two.', ''))
test_eq(cut(7, 8), MDX.replace('x   row one. row two.\n', ''))
test_eq(cut(4, 5, 6), MDX.replace('- Item one.\n- Item two.\n  Item two more.\n\n', ''))
P = 'Para one.\n\nB.\n\nPara three.\n'
test_eq([Rewrites(P, [('', md_parts(P))], [(k, k, '')]).new for k in range(3)], ['B.\n\nPara three.\n', 'Para one.\n\nPara three.\n', 'Para one.\n\nB.\n'])
print(cut(2, 3, 5))
```

[`review_diff`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_diff)
lists what you changed, by hand or with
[`review_apply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_apply).
It compares the file with the original that the first review saved.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L574"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### review_diff

``` python
def review_diff(
    path, # File that was reviewed and then edited
    out:NoneType=None, # Folder that `rewrite_review` wrote to; `review_dir(path)` if None
    n:NoneType=None, # Show only what changed during review `n`, counting from 1; every change since the first review if None
):
```

*What differs between the original that the first review saved and the
file at `path` now, or with `n` what changed during one review: the
file’s name, then each changed sentence or heading under its address, as
`-` lines and the `+` lines that replace them*

The diff starts with the file’s name and the number of changes. Each
change has the address of the text as it now stands, and a note when the
text is a docstring or in an exported Markdown cell, since a module
generated from the file then needs exporting again. The two sentences
that became one are shown together:

``` python
dif = review_diff(f, out)
assert dif.startswith(f'# {f}: 2 changes')
assert '(module docstring)\n- `make` builds a widget.\n- Finished widgets ride to the customer with `ship`.\n+ `make` builds a widget and `ship` posts it to the customer.' in dif
assert f'@{lnhash_at(f.read_text(), 21)} (docstring of `Widget.ship`)\n- The label carries the order number.\n+ The order number is printed on the label.' in dif
print(dif)
```

[`review_report`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_report)
writes the comparison again with a `NOW:` line for each run, which shows
the answers you took and those you left. It reports on the latest
review, or on review `n`. It reads that review’s copy of the file and
its replies, and writes the report beside them. It returns the counts
and the report’s file name, because the whole text is long. Pass
`full=True` to get the text.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L597"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### review_report

``` python
def review_report(
    path, # File that was reviewed and then edited
    out:NoneType=None, # Folder that `rewrite_review` wrote to; `review_dir(path)` if None
    full:bool=False, # Return the whole report, not only its counts and where it is?
    code:bool=False, # Show each notebook code cell under the first run that explains it?
    brief:bool=False, # Keep only the runs that a model asked about or that every model changed?
    n:NoneType=None, # Review to report on, counting from 1; the latest if None
):
```

*Write the
[`compare`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#compare)
text of one review of the file at `path`, with what each run of
sentences reads after editing, to that review’s folder; return its
counts and the file’s name, or the text with `full`*

The report starts with the counts. Sentence 7 is on line 22 of the file,
both models gave the same rewrite for it, and it was taken. So was the
second model’s answer for sentences 1 and 2. The last run reads as it
did:

``` python
rep = review_report(f, out, full=True)
assert rep.startswith('9 sentences. FIRST: 2 rewritten, 1 asked. SECOND: 2 rewritten, 0 asked. Edited: 2 of 3 runs.')
assert f"7 @{lnhash_at(SRC, 21)} ORIGINAL: The label carries the order number.\n  FIRST, SECOND [7]: The order number is printed on the label.\n  NOW: The order number is printed on the label." in rep
test_eq(rep.count('  NOW: -'), 1)
print(rep)
review_report(f, out)
```

Each review has a numbered folder of its own, so a second review keeps
the replies of the first. Here a second review of the edited file has
one reply with two rewrites, and
[`review_apply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_apply)
puts in one of them:

``` python
(d2 := out/'2').mkdir()
(d2/'widgets.reviewed.py').write_text(f.read_text())
(d2/'widgets.third.answer.txt').write_text('0 Widgets for a shop floor.\n7 `ship` raises `ValueError` when `addr` is empty.')
review_apply(f, {7: '`ship` raises `ValueError` when `addr` is empty.'}, out)
```

[`review_diff`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_diff)
with `n` shows what changed during one review. `n` counts the reviews
from 1, and a negative `n` counts back from the latest:

``` python
dif2 = review_diff(f, out, n=2)
assert dif2.startswith(f'# {f}: 1 change during review 2') and 'order number' not in dif2
assert '2 changes during review 1' in review_diff(f, out, n=1)
test_eq(review_diff(f, out, n=-1), dif2)
print(dif2)
```

[`review_pending`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_pending)
goes through every review. For each one it lists the runs that a model
rewrote or asked about and that still read as they did in that review.
Use it to find suggestions that nobody has acted on.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L614"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### review_pending

``` python
def review_pending(
    path, # File that has been reviewed
    out:NoneType=None, # Folder that `rewrite_review` wrote to; `review_dir(path)` if None
    code:bool=False, # Show each notebook code cell under the first run that explains it?
):
```

*For each review of the file at `path`, the runs that a model rewrote or
asked about and that still read as they did in that review: one
[`compare`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#compare)
text under a heading for each review*

Every run of the first review has been edited since. In the second
review, nobody has acted on the rewrite of sentence 0:

``` python
pend = review_pending(f, out)
r1,r2 = pend.split('# Review 2\n')
assert r1.startswith('# Review 1\n') and 'Shown: 0 of 3 runs.' in r1
assert 'Shown: 1 of 2 runs.' in r2 and 'ORIGINAL: Widgets for the shop floor.' in r2 and 'addr' not in r2
print(pend)
```

The models miss sentences. A docstring can read clearly beside the prose
that explains it and still be unclear on its own.
[`review_passed`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_passed)
lists the sentences of one review that no model rewrote or asked about,
without the code, for a person or an agent to read. It leaves out the
sentences that the models read without a number, which `mod_only` and
`skip` mark `[-]`. Each has the number that
[`review_apply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#review_apply)
takes and its address. A line names each docstring above its sentences.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/rewrite.py#L630"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### review_passed

``` python
def review_passed(
    path, # File that has been reviewed
    out:NoneType=None, # Folder that `rewrite_review` wrote to; `review_dir(path)` if None
    n:NoneType=None, # Review to read, counting from 1; the latest if None
):
```

*The numbered sentences that no model rewrote or asked about in one
review of the file at `path`: a count, then each as its number, address
and text, with a line that names each docstring*

In the first review, the two models between them rewrote or asked about
sentences 1, 2, 7 and 8. The other five are listed:

``` python
psd = review_passed(f, out, n=1)
assert psd.startswith('5 of 9 sentences that no model changed in review 1.')
assert 'Docstring of `make`:\n5 @' in psd and 'Build a widget from `spec`' in psd
assert 'order number' not in psd and 'def make' not in psd
print(psd)
```

`fresh=True` makes
[`rewrite_review`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#rewrite_review)
save the file as a new original.
[`_save_orig`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/rewrite.html#_save_orig)
first moves the original that it replaces into the folder of the latest
review, so that no saved text is lost. Here the file’s second review is
the latest:

``` python
orig = out/'widgets.orig.py'
_save_orig(f, orig, out/'2', fresh=True)
test_eq((out/'2'/'widgets.orig.py').read_text(), SRC)
test_eq(orig.read_text(), f.read_text())
```
